R-01.title: Requirements split across payments below a quotation or tender tier
R-01.description: Risk that a single requirement is met through several smaller payments to one supplier, so that the combined value crosses an App B tier that no single payment reaches, and the quotation, notice or tender steps for that tier are not run [rule:CPR-07] [rule:CPR-48] [rule:CPR-49] [rule:CPR-53].

likelihood.justification: In general procurement, {{$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.groups}} supplier groups [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.groups] have payments within a short window whose combined total crosses a tier that each payment stays under, including {{$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.per_threshold["25000"].groups}} groups at the three-quotes and notice tier [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.per_threshold["25000"].groups] and {{$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.per_threshold["500000"].groups}} at the App B row C boundary [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.per_threshold["500000"].groups]. The placement caveat does not explain general procurement groups. No test gives a flagged share of the scoped population, so L4 cannot be assessed; a share of general procurement suppliers in groups would settle it.

impact.justification: Table 1 Medium [history:IMP-3]: a requirement disaggregated to avoid the Rules or the Procurement Legislation [rule:CPR-07] gives a reasonable possibility of challenge where the aggregated value reaches the notice or tender tiers [rule:CPR-50] [rule:CPR-53].

evidence: General procurement groups crossing a tier: {{$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.groups}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.groups], combined value {{$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.total_gbp}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.general_procurement.total_gbp].
Premises groups: {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.premises.count}} [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.premises.count].
Anti-splitting rule, clause 6.16 [rule:CPR-07].
R-01.proposed_focus: Sample general procurement and premises groups from analytics-full/split_purchases.csv, prioritising groups at the three-quotes tier and the App B row C boundary; for each, establish whether the payments relate to one requirement and, if so, whether quotations, a notice or a tender were obtained at the aggregated value.

R-02.title: Order values set just under a quotation tier
R-02.description: Risk that order values are set just under an App B tier so that the one-quote or three-quotes steps are not triggered [rule:CPR-48] [rule:CPR-49] [rule:CPR-07].

likelihood.justification: In the procurement-relevant tags the band just under each tier is no fuller than the comparison band below it: general procurement ratio {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["1000"].by_tag.general_procurement.ratio_band_to_comparison}} at the one-quote tier [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["1000"].by_tag.general_procurement.ratio_band_to_comparison] and {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["25000"].by_tag.general_procurement.ratio_band_to_comparison}} at the three-quotes tier [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["25000"].by_tag.general_procurement.ratio_band_to_comparison]; premises {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["1000"].by_tag.premises.ratio_band_to_comparison}} [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["1000"].by_tag.premises.ratio_band_to_comparison]. A ratio above one in a procurement tag would raise this to L3.

impact.justification: Table 1 Minor [history:IMP-2]: values held under the one-quote or three-quotes tier mainly affect the internal quotation steps [rule:CPR-48] [rule:CPR-49], with a low possibility of legal challenge.

evidence: General procurement band-to-comparison ratio at the one-quote tier: {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["1000"].by_tag.general_procurement.ratio_band_to_comparison}} [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["1000"].by_tag.general_procurement.ratio_band_to_comparison].

General procurement band-to-comparison ratio at the three-quotes tier: {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["25000"].by_tag.general_procurement.ratio_band_to_comparison}} [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["25000"].by_tag.general_procurement.ratio_band_to_comparison].

Placements show a higher ratio at the one-quote tier, {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["1000"].by_tag.care_or_education_placement.ratio_band_to_comparison}} [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.counts.per_threshold["1000"].by_tag.care_or_education_placement.ratio_band_to_comparison]; placements are considered under R-07.
R-02.proposed_focus: Light-touch: in walkthroughs, confirm how order values near the App B tiers are set; sample a few general procurement payments from analytics-full/threshold_clustering.csv only if the walkthrough raises concerns.

R-03.title: Spend above the notice tier with no published contract notice
R-03.description: Risk that suppliers whose annualised spend enters the App B notice-publication tier are engaged without a published contract notice, written contract or recorded award approval [rule:CPR-50] [rule:CPR-52] [rule:CPR-27] [rule:CPR-45].

likelihood.justification: In general procurement, {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.no_notice_found.count}} suppliers above the notice tier [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.no_notice_found.count] have no exact-matched notice, {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.no_notice_found.share_of_population_annualised_estimate|pct}} of that tag's annualised estimate [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.no_notice_found.share_of_population_annualised_estimate]; premises {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.premises.no_notice_found.count}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.premises.no_notice_found.count]. The placement caveat does not cover these tags. The share comes from a test whose notices may be incomplete, so it cannot carry L4.

impact.justification: Table 1 Medium [history:IMP-3]: a contract in the notice tier let without a notice [rule:CPR-50] gives a reasonable possibility of successful legal challenge and of regulatory interest.

evidence: General procurement suppliers above the tier with no notice found: {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.no_notice_found.count}} of {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.population.count}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.general_procurement.population.count].
Agency staff suppliers above the tier with no notice found: {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.agency_staff.no_notice_found.count}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.agency_staff.no_notice_found.count].
Population for contract evidence requests: {{$.tests.high_value_suppliers.counts.suppliers}} suppliers enter the three-quotes tier [metric:$.tests.high_value_suppliers.counts.suppliers].
Contract Letting audit, Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-01].
R-03.proposed_focus: Sample general procurement, premises and agency staff suppliers from analytics-full/off_contract.csv (no notice found), and resolve analytics-full/off_contract_candidates.csv first; for each, request the contract, the quotations or tender, the notice (Contracts Finder or the Central Digital Platform) and the award approval, using analytics-full/high_value_suppliers.csv as the request population. Check whether a framework, waiver or App C exclusion applies before treating any item as an exception.

R-04.title: Spend continuing after a contract notice has ended
R-04.description: Risk that payments continue to suppliers after their contract has ended without an approved extension [rule:CPR-58].

likelihood.justification: Of {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.exact_matched_suppliers_paid}} exact-matched suppliers paid in the window [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.exact_matched_suppliers_paid], {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.flagged}} [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.flagged] have only notices that ended before the window, all in general procurement ({{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.by_tag.general_procurement.count}}) [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.by_tag.general_procurement.count] and premises ({{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.by_tag.premises.count}}) [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.by_tag.premises.count]. The missing-notices caveat keeps this at L3 at most.

impact.justification: Table 1 Minor [history:IMP-2]: where the contract provides for extension, the control at issue is the internal S151 Officer approval [rule:CPR-58], giving a low possibility of legal challenge; the value involved is {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.totals_gbp.flagged_window_total}} in the window [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.totals_gbp.flagged_window_total].

evidence: Suppliers flagged: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.flagged}} [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.counts.flagged].
Window spend with these suppliers: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.totals_gbp.flagged_window_total}} [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.totals_gbp.flagged_window_total].
R-04.proposed_focus: Test every supplier in analytics-full/expired_notice_spend.csv: request the extension and its S151 Officer approval, or a newer contract and its notice.

R-05.title: Spend beyond the awarded contract value
R-05.description: Risk that spend with a contracted supplier runs beyond the awarded value without an approved variation [rule:CPR-59] [rule:CPR-60].

likelihood.justification: Of {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.population}} suppliers with one live single-supplier notice and an award value [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.population], {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.flagged}} [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.flagged] have an annualised estimate at or above the flag ratio of the award per year, mainly in general procurement ({{$.tests.spend_vs_award.by_tag.general_procurement.count}}) [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.by_tag.general_procurement.count]. The flagged share is below the pervasive level, so L4 does not apply.

impact.justification: Table 1 Medium [history:IMP-3]: a variation above the Threshold needs board approval [rule:CPR-60], and an unapproved increase in scope gives a reasonable possibility of successful legal challenge.

evidence: Flagged suppliers: {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.flagged}} [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.counts.flagged], window spend {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.totals_gbp.flagged_window_total}} [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.totals_gbp.flagged_window_total].
Variation approvals, App C row E [rule:CPR-59] [rule:CPR-60].
R-05.proposed_focus: Test every supplier in analytics-full/spend_vs_award.csv: request the contract value, any variations and their approvals; note that award values may be estimates or maxima.

R-06.title: Duplicate payments to the same supplier
R-06.description: Risk that the same invoice or amount is paid more than once to a supplier, leading to overpayment that is not recovered [history:AUD-11].

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.duplicates.counts.by_class.different_timestamp.pairs}} same-supplier, same-amount pairs within the duplicate window have different timestamps [metric:$.tests.duplicates.counts.by_class.different_timestamp.pairs], including {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.general_procurement.count}} in general procurement [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.general_procurement.count] and {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.premises.count}} in premises [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.premises.count]. Most pairs are placements, which the caveat explains as recurring fixed-rate payments; the procurement-tag pairs are not explained by it.

impact.justification: Table 1 Critical [history:IMP-5]: the repeat value beyond the first payment in clusters with different timestamps [metric:$.tests.duplicates.totals_gbp.repeat_value_beyond_first_clusters_with_different_timestamp] is the money that could be lost if those repeats were not valid. It is a ceiling across all tags, most of it in placements where repeats are often legitimate.

evidence: Different-timestamp pairs: {{$.tests.duplicates.counts.by_class.different_timestamp.pairs}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.counts.by_class.different_timestamp.pairs].
Placement pairs: {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count].
Accounts Payable audit, Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-11].
R-06.proposed_focus: Sample different-timestamp clusters from analytics-full/duplicates_clusters.csv, all general procurement and premises clusters first, then the largest placement clusters; for each, match the payments to distinct invoices or to a recurring schedule, and confirm recovery of any repeat payment.

R-07.title: Care and education placements arranged without the App C records and approvals
R-07.description: Risk that placements and care packages arranged outside competition under App C lack the recorded reasons for provider choice, the PSR process or the board approval that App C requires [rule:CPR-56] [rule:CPR-61] [rule:CPR-62].

likelihood.justification: Placements show many flagged items, {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.no_notice_found.count}} suppliers above the notice tier with no notice [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.no_notice_found.count] and {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count}} split-purchase groups [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count], but the analytics caveats explain these routinely: placements are often arranged under App C exclusions or frameworks and recur. No test measures whether the App C records exist; a case-file sample would.

impact.justification: Table 1 Minor [history:IMP-2]: the requirement is to record reasons on case notes [rule:CPR-61] and obtain board approval above the Threshold [rule:CPR-62]; gaps give a low possibility of legal challenge. The Purchase of Residential and Nursing Care Provision audit gave Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-14].

evidence: Placement suppliers above the notice tier with no notice: {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.no_notice_found.count}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.no_notice_found.count].
Purchase of Residential and Nursing Care Provision, Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-14].
App C row F, records of provider choice [rule:CPR-61].
R-07.proposed_focus: Sample placement suppliers from analytics-full/off_contract.csv (care_or_education_placement) and confirm the App C basis: case-note reasons for provider choice, the PSR record where applicable, framework call-off or board approval above the Threshold.

impact.justification: Table 1 Minor [history:IMP-2]: the main exposure is to the written-contract and notice requirements [rule:CPR-27] [rule:CPR-50] for grant agreements, with a low possibility of legal challenge.

evidence: Grant recipients above the tier with no notice found: {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.no_notice_found.count}} of {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.population.count}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.population.count].

R-08.proposed_focus: Sample grant recipients from analytics-full/off_contract.csv (grant tag) and request the grant agreement, the basis for award (competition, exclusion or exception) and its approval.

evidence: Waiver grounds and approvals, clause 7.2 and clause 7.5 [rule:CPR-13] [rule:CPR-21].
Contracts & Partnerships source of risk [history:THM-21].

R-06.description: Risk that the same invoice or amount is paid more than once to a supplier, leading to overpayment that is not recovered [history:AUD-11].

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.duplicates.counts.by_class.different_timestamp.pairs}} same-supplier, same-amount pairs within the duplicate window have different timestamps [metric:$.tests.duplicates.counts.by_class.different_timestamp.pairs], including {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.general_procurement.count}} in general procurement [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.general_procurement.count] and {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.premises.count}} in premises [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.premises.count]. Most pairs are placements, which the caveat explains as recurring fixed-rate payments; the procurement-tag pairs are not explained by it.

impact.justification: Table 1 Critical [history:IMP-5]: the repeat value beyond the first payment in clusters with different timestamps [metric:$.tests.duplicates.totals_gbp.repeat_value_beyond_first_clusters_with_different_timestamp] is the money that could be lost if those repeats were not valid. It is a ceiling across all tags, most of it in placements where repeats are often legitimate.

override.note: Auditor (Allen Cao, 2026-10-16) lowered impact: the loss figure is a ceiling and most repeated amounts are care and education placements, which often recur legitimately

evidence: Different-timestamp pairs: {{$.tests.duplicates.counts.by_class.different_timestamp.pairs}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.counts.by_class.different_timestamp.pairs].
Placement pairs: {{$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count}} [metric:$.tests.duplicates.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count].
Accounts Payable audit, Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-11].
R-06.proposed_focus: Sample different-timestamp clusters from analytics-full/duplicates_clusters.csv, all general procurement and premises clusters first, then the largest placement clusters; for each, match the payments to distinct invoices or to a recurring schedule, and confirm recovery of any repeat payment.

R-07.title: Care and education placements arranged without the App C records and approvals
R-07.description: Risk that placements and care packages arranged outside competition under App C lack the recorded reasons for provider choice, the PSR process or the board approval that App C requires [rule:CPR-56] [rule:CPR-61] [rule:CPR-62].

likelihood.justification: Placements show many flagged items, {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.no_notice_found.count}} suppliers above the notice tier with no notice [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.no_notice_found.count] and {{$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count}} split-purchase groups [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.count], but the analytics caveats explain these routinely: placements are often arranged under App C exclusions or frameworks and recur. No test measures whether the App C records exist; a case-file sample would.

impact.justification: Table 1 Minor [history:IMP-2]: the requirement is to record reasons on case notes [rule:CPR-61] and obtain board approval above the Threshold [rule:CPR-62]; gaps give a low possibility of legal challenge. The Purchase of Residential and Nursing Care Provision audit gave Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-14].

evidence: Placement suppliers above the notice tier with no notice: {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.no_notice_found.count}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.care_or_education_placement.no_notice_found.count].
Purchase of Residential and Nursing Care Provision, Reasonable Assurance [history:AUD-14].
App C row F, records of provider choice [rule:CPR-61].
R-07.proposed_focus: Sample placement suppliers from analytics-full/off_contract.csv (care_or_education_placement) and confirm the App C basis: case-note reasons for provider choice, the PSR record where applicable, framework call-off or board approval above the Threshold.

R-08.title: Grants awarded without the procurement steps that apply to contracts
R-08.description: Risk that grants, which clause 1.6.2 treats as contracts, are awarded above the notice tier without a published notice, written agreement or recorded approval [rule:CPR-50] [rule:CPR-27].

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.no_notice_found.count}} grant recipients above the notice tier [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.no_notice_found.count] have no exact-matched notice, with {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.exact_match_any_notice.count}} matched [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.exact_match_any_notice.count]. No analytics caveat gives a routine explanation for grants. The missing-notices caveat keeps this at L3 at most.

impact.justification: Table 1 Minor [history:IMP-2]: the main exposure is to the written-contract and notice requirements [rule:CPR-27] [rule:CPR-50] for grant agreements, with a low possibility of legal challenge.

evidence: Grant recipients above the tier with no notice found: {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.no_notice_found.count}} of {{$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.population.count}} [metric:$.tests.off_contract.by_tag.grant.population.count].
Written contract requirement, clause 10.2 [rule:CPR-27].
R-08.proposed_focus: Sample grant recipients from analytics-full/off_contract.csv (grant tag) and request the grant agreement, the basis for award (competition, exclusion or exception) and its approval.

R-09.title: Exceptions and waivers of competition not documented or approved
R-09.description: Risk that competition is waived above the three-quotes tier without a valid ground, a written exception report or the S151 Officer and Monitoring Officer approvals [rule:CPR-13] [rule:CPR-15] [rule:CPR-19] [rule:CPR-21].

likelihood.justification: No analytics test measures waivers; the risk rests on the rules [rule:CPR-13] [rule:CPR-19] and on the Contracts & Partnerships source of risk in the Risk Management Strategy [history:THM-21]. Unmatched suppliers under R-03 may rely on waivers, which the audit would test.

impact.justification: Table 1 Medium [history:IMP-3]: a waiver above the tier without a valid ground [rule:CPR-13] gives a reasonable possibility of successful legal challenge.

evidence: Waiver grounds and approvals, clause 7.2 and clause 7.5 [rule:CPR-13] [rule:CPR-21].
Contracts & Partnerships source of risk [history:THM-21].
R-09.proposed_focus: Obtain the waiver and exception register for the period; test a sample for a valid ground, the written exception report and the approvals; cross-match waivers to the R-03 sample.
